Drumming regional variation: pdfas, repdfas, glmms statistics

Vesta Eleuteri

2025-04-04

  • Introduction
  • Preliminaries
  • Descriptives
  • Analyses for regional variation in drumming structure
  • Subspecies drumming measures stability over time
  • Analyses for regional variation in drumming onset during pant-hoot
  • References

Introduction

This document accompanies the manuscript “Chimpanzee drumming shows rhythmicity and subspecies variation” Vesta Eleuteri et al. (2025).

Here we tested for regional variation in drumming by comparing drumming structure across communities, across populations, and between subspecies. We first used permuted discriminant function analyses (pDFA) to test for the group differences and then used repeated discriminant function analyses (repDFA) and generalized linear mixed models (glmms) to identify the key variables discriminating the groups in significant pDFAs.

Here we also tested for regional variation in drumming behaviour by comparing the timing of drumming onset during pant-hoot vocalizations across communities, across populations, and between subspecies. We used glmms to test for the group differences.

Descriptives

Descriptives drumming measures community

descriptives_com <- xdata %>%
  group_by(Subspecies, Population, Community) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Number_Drums = n(),
    Mean_N_hits = round(mean(N_hits, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_N_hits = round(sd(N_hits, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Mean_Bout_Duration = round(mean(Total_bout_duration, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_Bout_Duration = round(sd(Total_bout_duration, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Mean_Bout_cv = round(mean(Bout_cv, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_Bout_cv = round(sd(Bout_cv, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Mean_Bout_npvi = round(mean(Bout_npvi, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_Bout_npvi = round(sd(Bout_npvi, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    Mean_Entropy = round(mean(Bout_entropy, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    SD_Entropy = round(sd(Bout_entropy, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
kable(descriptives_com, format = "html", caption = "Descriptives drumming measures community") %>%
  kable_styling("striped", full_width = FALSE)

Analyses for regional variation in drumming structure

Sort data

Community pDFA

We first tested for regional variation using a pDFA to compare drumming structure across communities.

set.seed(131)
pdfa.res.communities <- pDFA.nested(
  test.fac = "Pop_com_code", contr.fac = "Com_indiv_code",
  variables = c(
    "log.Total_bout_duration_c", "log.N_hits_c",
    "Bout_cv_c", "Bout_npvi_c", "Bout_entropy_c"
  ),
  restrict.by = NULL,
  n.contr.fac.levels.to.sel = NULL,
  n.to.sel.per.contr.fac.level = NULL, n.sel = 100, n.perm = 1000,
  pdfa.data = xdata
)

Communtiy repDFA

set.seed(5)
ImpVars_all_comms_allvabs <- repDFA_nested(xdata,
  testfactor = "Pop_com_code",
  balancefactor = c("Pop_com_code", "Com_indiv_code"),
  varnames = c(
    "log.Total_bout_duration_c", "log.N_hits_c",
    "Bout_cv_c", "Bout_npvi_c", "Bout_entropy_c"
  ),
  npercomb = 3, nrand = 1000
)

The repDFA identified as key variables on discriminant 1: nPVI and Number of hits, on discriminant 2: total bout duration and entropy. We thus used glmms to test if these variables significantly vary across the communities.

Community glmm nPVI

## Run model
Model_npvi <- lmer(Bout_npvi_c ~ Community + (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata, REML = F)

## Full-null model comparison
null_Model_npvi <- lmer(Bout_npvi_c ~ (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata, REML = F)
Chisq_Model_npvi <- as.data.frame(anova(null_Model_npvi, Model_npvi, test = "Chisq")) 
Chisq_Model_npvi <- round(Chisq_Model_npvi, 3)
Chisq_Model_npvi
                npar      AIC      BIC    logLik -2*log(L)  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
null_Model_npvi    3 3741.514 3753.263 -1867.757  3735.514     NA NA         NA
Model_npvi        13 3732.256 3783.167 -1853.128  3706.256 29.258 10      0.001

nPVI significantly varies across communities.

Confirmatory Subspecies pDFA

Because plots suggest that the variation lies across communities of different subspecies, we followed up the community comparison with a pDFA comparing the two subspecies (eastern and western).

set.seed(126)

  test.fac = "Subspecies", contr.fac = "Com_indiv_code",

    "log.Total_bout_duration_c", "log.N_hits_c",

  n.contr.fac.levels.to.sel = NULL,

)

The repDFA idenfitied as most contributing variables on discriminant 1: nPVI and number of hits. We thus used glmms to test if these variables significantly discriminate the subspecies.

Subspecies glmm nPVI

## Run model
Model_npvi_sub <- lmer(Bout_npvi_c ~ Subspecies + (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata, REML = F)

## Full-null model comparison
null_Model_npvi_sub <- lmer(Bout_npvi_c ~ (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata, REML = F)
Chisq_Model_npvi_sub <- as.data.frame(anova(null_Model_npvi_sub, Model_npvi_sub, test = "Chisq")) # sig
Chisq_Model_npvi_sub <- round(Chisq_Model_npvi_sub, 3)
Chisq_Model_npvi_sub
                    npar      AIC      BIC    logLik -2*log(L)  Chisq Df
null_Model_npvi_sub    3 3741.514 3753.263 -1867.757  3735.514     NA NA
Model_npvi_sub         4 3717.897 3733.562 -1854.949  3709.897 25.617  1
                    Pr(>Chisq)
null_Model_npvi_sub         NA
Model_npvi_sub               0

nPVI significantly varies between subspecies.

Subspecies glmm number of hits

Model_nhits_sub <- lmer(log.N_hits_c ~ Subspecies + (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata, REML = F)

Chisq_Model_nhits_sub <- as.data.frame(anova(null_Model_nhits_sub, Model_nhits_sub, test = "Chisq")) # sig
Chisq_Model_nhits_sub <- round(Chisq_Model_nhits_sub, 3)

null_Model_nhits_sub         NA

Number of hits also significantly varies between subspecies.

Taken together, our results above show that -across both communities and subspecies- western chimpanzees drum with lower nPVI (i.e., variability between adjacent pairs of inter-hit intervals) and more hits in drumming bouts that eastern chimpanzees.

Across subspecies Populations pDFA

Because the sampled populations live in different habitat types, we used another pDFA to test whether ecology might affect drumming by comparing drumming structure across populations.

set.seed(128)
pdfa.res.populations <- pDFA.nested(
  test.fac = "Population", contr.fac = "Com_indiv_code",
  variables = c(
    "log.Total_bout_duration_c", "log.N_hits_c",
    "Bout_cv_c", "Bout_npvi_c", "Bout_entropy_c"
  ), restrict.by = NULL,
  n.contr.fac.levels.to.sel = NULL,
  n.to.sel.per.contr.fac.level = NULL, n.sel = 100, n.perm = 1000,
  pdfa.data = xdata
)

The pDFA is non-significant showing that drumming structure does not vary across all populations and thus suggesting that ecology may not impact drumming structure.

But because the populations belong to different subspecies, we further assessed whether ecology may affect drumming structure while controlling for subspecies variation. We used two additional pDFAs comparing populations within each subspecies.

Western populations pDFA

  n.contr.fac.levels.to.sel = NULL,

Subspecies drumming measures stability over time

Here we test whether the drumming measures remain stable over time within the subspecies

# convert recording date to datetime object
xdata$Recording_date <- as.Date(xdata$Date, format = "%d.%m.%y")

Distribution of recording dates

ggplot(xdata, aes(x = Recording_date, fill = Subspecies, colour = Subspecies)) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.6, binwidth = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
    theme_drumming() +
    labs(x = "Recording date", y = "Counts", title = "Number of bouts by recording date") +
    facet_wrap(~Subspecies, ncol = 1) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

Statistics

Does nPVI remain stable across time?

# nPVI
ggplot(xdata, aes(x = Recording_date, y = Bout_npvi, color = Subspecies)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", show.legend = FALSE) +
    theme_drumming() +
    labs(x = "Recording date", y = "nPVI", title = "Stability of nPVI over recording dates") +
    facet_wrap(~Subspecies, ncol = 1) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggsave(here("plots", "stability_npvi.svg"), width = 10, height = 10)
ggsave(here("plots", "stability_npvi.png"), width = 10, height = 10)
mod <- lmer(Bout_npvi ~ Days_before_2024 * Subspecies + (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata, REML = FALSE)
red <- lmer(Bout_npvi ~ Days_before_2024 + Subspecies + (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata, REML = FALSE)
chisq.npvi <- as.data.frame(anova(red, mod, test = "chisq"))
chisq.npvi
    npar      AIC      BIC    logLik -2*log(L)     Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)
red    5 3719.605 3739.186 -1854.803  3709.605        NA NA         NA
mod    6 3721.025 3744.522 -1854.512  3709.025 0.5804957  1  0.4461181

nPVI remains stable across time within subspecies.

Analyses for regional variation in drumming onset during pant-hoot

We last tested for regional variation in drumming behaviour using 3 glmms to compare the timing of drumming onset during pant-hoot vocalizations across communities, across populations, and between subspecies.

Sort data

levels(xdata$With_Ph)[levels(xdata$With_Ph) %in% c("with")] <- "With"
xdata_ph <- subset(xdata, Start_Ph %in% c("Build-Up", "Climax", "Let-Down", "roar", "Roar")) # keeping only drums starting in clear pant-hoot phases
xdata_ph <- droplevels(xdata_ph)
xdata_ph$Start_Ph <- factor(xdata_ph$Start_Ph) # conver to factor
levels(xdata_ph$Start_Ph)[levels(xdata_ph$Start_Ph) %in% c("Build-Up", "roar", "Roar")] <- "Before Climax Start" # rename level
levels(xdata_ph$Start_Ph)[levels(xdata_ph$Start_Ph) %in% c("Climax", "Let-Down")] <- "After Climax Start" # rename level

## Check frequencies of response variable
table(xdata_ph$Start_Ph, xdata_ph$Community) # South has 0 drums After Climax Start so remove level
xdata_ph <- subset(xdata_ph, Community != c("South")) # removed, n=302
xdata_ph <- droplevels(xdata_ph) # drop levels no observations
table(xdata_ph$Start_Ph, xdata_ph$Community)

## Dummy code response variable
xdata_ph$Start_Ph <- as.numeric(xdata_ph$Start_Ph == "Before Climax Start") # Dummy coded Before Climax Start as 1

Community glmm

## Run model
Model_start_ph_com <- glmer(Start_Ph ~ Community + (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata_ph, family = binomial)

## Full-null model comparison
null_Model_start_ph_com <- glmer(Start_Ph ~ (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata_ph, family = binomial)
Chisq_Model_start_ph_com <- as.data.frame(anova(null_Model_start_ph_com, Model_start_ph_com, test = "Chisq")) # sig
Chisq_Model_start_ph_com <- round(Chisq_Model_start_ph_com, 3)
Chisq_Model_start_ph_com
                        npar     AIC     BIC   logLik -2*log(L)  Chisq Df
null_Model_start_ph_com    2 306.177 313.598 -151.088   302.177     NA NA
Model_start_ph_com        11 305.514 346.329 -141.757   283.514 18.663  9
                        Pr(>Chisq)
null_Model_start_ph_com         NA
Model_start_ph_com           0.028

The timing of drumming onset significantly varies across communities.

Population glmm

## Run model
Model_start_ph_pop <- glmer(Start_Ph ~ Population + (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata_ph, family = binomial)

## Full-null model comparison
null_Model_start_ph_pop <- glmer(Start_Ph ~ (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata_ph, family = binomial)
Chisq_Model_start_ph_pop <- as.data.frame(anova(null_Model_start_ph_pop, Model_start_ph_pop, test = "Chisq"))
Chisq_Model_start_ph_pop <- round(Chisq_Model_start_ph_pop, 3)
Chisq_Model_start_ph_pop
                        npar     AIC     BIC   logLik -2*log(L) Chisq Df
null_Model_start_ph_pop    2 306.177 313.598 -151.088   302.177    NA NA
Model_start_ph_pop         7 301.537 327.510 -143.768   287.537 14.64  5
                        Pr(>Chisq)
null_Model_start_ph_pop         NA
Model_start_ph_pop           0.012

The timing of drumming onset significantly varies across all populations.

Confirmatory subspecies glmm

## Run model
Model_start_ph_sub <- glmer(Start_Ph ~ Subspecies + (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata_ph, family = binomial)

## Full-null model comparison
null_Model_start_ph_sub <- glmer(Start_Ph ~ (1 | Com_indiv_code), data = xdata_ph, family = binomial)
Chisq_Model_start_ph_sub <- as.data.frame(anova(null_Model_start_ph_sub, Model_start_ph_sub, test = "Chisq"))
Chisq_Model_start_ph_sub <- round(Chisq_Model_start_ph_sub, 3)
Chisq_Model_start_ph_sub
                        npar     AIC     BIC   logLik -2*log(L) Chisq Df
null_Model_start_ph_sub    2 306.177 313.598 -151.088   302.177    NA NA
Model_start_ph_sub         3 293.797 304.928 -143.898   287.797 14.38  1
                        Pr(>Chisq)
null_Model_start_ph_sub         NA
Model_start_ph_sub               0

The timing of drumming onset significantly varies between subspecies.

Taken together, we find that western chimpanzees start to drum earlier in the pant-hoot than eastern chimpanzees typically during the build-up phase.
